title: CAM-ICU (Delirium Assessment)
sources: Ely EW et al. JAMA 2001; SCCM PADIS 2018 guideline
purpose: A structured bedside screen for delirium in the ICU patient, usable in the intubated / non-verbal. First check arousal with RASS: if RASS is −4 or −5 the patient is unarousable — CAM-ICU cannot be completed, recheck later. Otherwise assess the four features below.

items.label: Feature 1 — Acute onset OR fluctuating course of mental status (vs. baseline, or fluctuation in the last 24 h by RASS/GCS/prior CAM-ICU)
Feature 2 — Inattention: Letters ('SAVEAHAART' — squeeze on A) or Pictures; ≥ 3 errors = present
Feature 3 — Altered level of consciousness: current RASS anything other than 0 (calm and alert)
Feature 4 — Disorganised thinking: 4 yes/no questions + a 2-step command; ≥ 2 errors = present (only assessed if Feature 3 is absent)

interpretation.label: CAM-ICU NEGATIVE — delirium not detected at this assessment (requires Feature 1 AND Feature 2, plus either Feature 3 or Feature 4). Continue routine screening at least once per shift and with any mental-status change

Check the rule: CAM-ICU is POSITIVE only if Feature 1 + Feature 2 are both present AND (Feature 3 OR Feature 4) is present. If so → DELIRIUM. Act on it: search for causes (sepsis, hypoxia, hypercapnia, metabolic, drugs — esp. benzodiazepines and anticholinergics, withdrawal, pain, urinary retention), stop/minimise deliriogenic drugs, target light sedation, mobilise, restore day–night cycle, reorient, ensure glasses/hearing aids. Antipsychotics do not shorten delirium — reserve for dangerous agitation

notes: The point tally here is a helper only — apply the diagnostic rule: (1 AND 2) AND (3 OR 4). The ICDSC is an alternative 8-item screen (≥ 4 = delirium). CAM-ICU does not grade severity or distinguish hypoactive (the common, easily-missed, worse-prognosis form) from hyperactive. Pair with the ABCDEF bundle.
buildNote: Diagnostic rule (1 AND 2) AND (3 OR 4); additive sum is a helper, not the diagnosis.
